sentences.text: Present: Mr. S.K.S. Bedi, Advocate for the applicant.

Crm-15952-2016 Application is allowed as prayed for.
Crm-15953-2016
This order of mine shall dispose of application filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for release of the applicant from jail in lieu of the deposit of balance amount of fine.

While disposing of the revision filed by the present applicant against his sentence awarded for the commission of offence punishable under Section 16(1)(c) of the Prevention of Food and Adulteration Act, 1954, this Court passed the order dated 17.07.2009 in CRR No.253 of 2000 and observed as under:
"Keeping in view the peculiarity of the facts and circumstances of the case, the sentence of the petitioner is reduced to the already undergone (1 month and 6 days).
The fine imposed by the learned trial Court upon the petitioner is enhanced to Rs.5,000/-.

entities.text: Prevention of Food and Adulteration Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The difference of fine shall be deposited by the petitioner in the trial Court within two months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.

If the petitioner failed to deposit this amount within the aforesaid period,
this revision petition shall be deemed to have been dismissed and the trial Court itself being the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate shall take necessary steps to send the petitioner to jail to serve the unexpired period of his sentence.

The Registry is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the successor Court of Mr. Satish Ahlawat, the then Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kaithal."
1 of 3

It comes out that the enhanced amount of fine of `4,000/- was not paid and therefore, the default clause became operative and revision should have been deemed to be dismissed w.e.f. 2 months after July 17, 2009.
It also comes out that an application was filed by the applicant for recalling the said order in the year 2016.

The same was dismissed on 29.04.2016 and the following order was passed:
"Present: Mr. Anand Kumar Bishnoi, Advocate for the applicant-petitioner.
It comes out that the order was passed in the year 2009.

Therefore, after seven years,
there is no ground to extend the time to pay the fine.
Dismissed."
Still not satisfied, another application was filed for recalling the order dated 29.04.2016 for deposit of balance amount of fine of `4,000/-, which was dismissed by the court on May 09, 2016.

Now, the Rajinder Pal vs State Of Haryana on 18 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70094974/
1 present application has been filed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the balance amount of fine has been deposited and receipt of the same is attached with the application.
It is further contended by the counsel for the applicant that the brother of the applicant was pursuing the litigation on behalf of the applicant and was in contact with him.
Later on, he suffered paralytic attack in brain and lost his memory.
Therefore, the letter sent by the counsel was not responded.
Accordingly, the applicant did not come to know about the order passed by this Court as he had 2 of 3 shifted to some other place.
The order was passed seven years back.
It was the duty of the applicant to enquire about the fate of the revision.
The mere fact that the applicant has been shifted to some other place is not a ground to recall the order.
Further the brother of the applicant became insane after the passing of the order and releasing the applicant-petitioner.
In these circumstances, there is no ground to recall the order.
Hence, dismissed.
(KULDIP SINGH)
May 18, 2016 JUDGE sarita
